title: Connect {{provider}} in four steps
stepApp: Open the OAuth application page and create an application.

appHint.gitlab: Under User Settings, Applications. A group or admin application works too.
appHint.gitea: Under Settings, Applications, Manage OAuth2 Applications. Tick Confidential Client.
appHint.forgejo: Under Settings, Applications, Manage OAuth2 Applications. Tick Confidential Client.
appHint.bitbucket: Open the workspace, then Settings, OAuth consumers, Add consumer. Tick This is a private consumer.

stepRedirect: Set the redirect URI (callback URL) to exactly this value.
copyFailed: Could not copy. Select the URI and copy it by hand.
scopesNone: This provider has no scope list. Grant repository read and write when it asks.
stepPaste: Paste the client ID and secret below, then save and authorize.

hint.https: This address is HTTPS, so the provider will accept it as a redirect URI.
hint.loopback: This is a local address. Most providers accept it for testing from this browser only.
hint.insecure: This address is plain HTTP and most providers refuse it as a redirect URI. Use HTTPS or connect with a token.

fallback.title: Cannot use OAuth here?
fallback.body: A token needs no redirect URI, no public domain and no application.

field.whitespace: Remove the spaces or line breaks from the pasted value.
field.unusual: This does not look like a typical {{provider}} value. Check you copied the whole thing.

methods.title: Ways to connect
methods.selfManaged: Self-managed GitLab works with every method: enter your base URL in the connect panel.

oauth.name: OAuth application
oauth.unlocks: Sign in through the provider. Unlocks repositories, webhooks, status and comments, and refreshes by itself.

token.name: Access token
token.unlocks: Paste a personal, project or group token. No redirect URI or public domain needed.

deploy_token.name: Deploy token
deploy_token.unlocks: Read-only registry pulls (read_registry) for deploying images.

ci_job.name: CI job token or OIDC
ci_job.unlocks: Let pipeline jobs deploy without a stored secret.

access.scopesUnknown: The control plane does not report the granted scopes for this account yet, so each feature shows Not reported.
access.addScopeMissing: Needs an endpoint that upgrades scopes. For now, re-authorize or add a token with more scopes.
access.rotateOauth: OAuth connections renew themselves, so there is no token to rotate.
access.rotateUnsupported: This provider cannot rotate this credential. Add a new token and disconnect the old one.

import.title: Import repositories
import.body: Pick repositories or a whole group and turn them into apps.

previews.title: Enable merge request previews
previews.body: Deploy a preview for each open merge request.

ci.title: Add CI trust
ci.body: Let pipeline jobs deploy with a short-lived identity.

webhook.title: Add a webhook
webhook.body: Send deploy and build events to another service.

registry.title: Connect a registry
registry.body: Store pull credentials for private images.

rotate.title: Rotate the token for {{label}}?
rotate.description: This replaces the access token on the provider.
rotate.consequence: GitLab issues a new token and the old one stops working at once. Builds and pulls that use this connection switch over automatically.
rotate.expiryHint: Prefilled from the {{days}} day rotation lifetime. Clear it to let the provider decide.

errors.noMasterKey: Rotation needs a master key on the control plane. Set one up under encryption keys, then try again.
errors.provider: The provider did not complete the rotation. The current token is unchanged, try again in a moment.
errors.badDate: Use a date in YYYY-MM-DD format.

toast.noExpiry: The provider reported no expiry for the new token.
